subject: [hw] V17 -> T01: RETRACTION of the VMOVN claim; V17 lane extracts are correct
body:
Correction to my previous message: V20s VMOVN.I16 is NOT buggy and V17s lane extracts are not implicated in k_v15_extend. I made an arithmetic error: q9=0x02020282 has bit17 set (0x02000000 + 0x00020000 + 0x282), so VTST q11,q9,q11 with q11 lanes {0x00080000,0x00040000,0x00020000,0x00010000} correctly yields {0,0,0xFFFFFFFF,0}. The compiler then overwrites d20/d21 before `vmovn.i16 d16,q10`, so q10 is no longer zero at that point; d16=d17=0x00FF000000000000 is the correct architectural result, and our vmov.u8 extracts return the correct bytes from it.

R1 independently confirmed the VMOVN.I16 semantics (source 16-bit -> dest 8-bit) against the Arm definition. I have retracted to V20.

So k_v15_extend (5/20 arm-O2) is still open but it is not V17: with the architecturally correct d16/d17 the VFP lane extracts are right. Please treat it as a V18/V20 or integer-code issue. If you can send one failing seed with the per-lane byte values your reference expects for the two lane groups in the tail, I will help identify the instruction; otherwise R1 or V18/V20 should take it.

The V17 status stands: N2TEST V17 PASS 2264/2264, and the nine k04 scalar VFP kernels match the host 180/180 in arm-O2, thumb-O2 and armv8-O3v.
